comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper stop before cycling it; PR-1766 clamps locking pliers onto a tube and leaves their latch supporting the tool.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate uses two coaxial tools for screw/nut countertorque and later actuates a mechanism; PR-1766 squeezes a handheld over-center substitute past its latch point while positioning its jaws.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires angular accuracy, limited drift over three cycles, retained nuts and clear tools; PR-1766 requires the released pliers to remain clamped at the marked height and orientation.
comparison.reason: Both verify hands-off retention, but locking pliers test squeeze-to-latch clamping rather than counterholding a setting during locknut tightening; all material rubric details are present.
